_summary.written_by: round two translation pass over data/translation_worklist_2.json; PROPOSAL, not ratified. data/prompt_categorisation.json was NOT modified. Conventions and vocabulary inherited from scripts/f13_chinese_prompts.py and data/chinese_translations.json (round one).

definitions.slot_preserved: the continuation slot is open in the same grammatical position and admits the same kind of word as the English. False means the KIND changed, not that the Chinese is merely less idiomatic.
definitions.pair_minimal: true iff the two members differ in exactly one contiguous span AND that span is a single lexical substitution corresponding to the declared contrast. 'n/a' means minimality was never the claim: the prompt is ungrouped, or belongs to a single-role POOL rather than a contrast, or its English pair is not minimal either. 122 of 139 are n/a this round because 47 prompts are ungrouped and a further 62 sit in nine pools.
definitions.verification: machine-checked: coverage against the worklist (139/139, no extras), greedy longest-match segmentation of every string against data/dict/jieba_dict_big.txt (0 characters outside the dictionary), POLE_A-before-POLE_B index comparison in every BOTH cell in Chinese AND in the English source (3/3 pass in both languages), prefix/suffix diff for every two-member group, duplicate detection inside round two, against round one's 217, and against every language=zh record in data/prompt_categorisation.json, and a check that no prompt ends on punctuation.

f11_species.failure: BOTH cell cannot be formed without an added head noun
f11_species.detail: The design needs a cell holding 'human' and 'animal' at once. Chinese has no endocentric noun-noun compound for it. The only available compound, 人兽, reads as bestiality in modern usage and would pull the ACT slot into a sexual register the English compound does not carry; 半人半兽 resolves the contradiction into a partition (half each) instead of holding it, which is the opposite of what F11 measures, and it replaces the pole term 动物 with 兽 so a coder searching the pole terms finds nothing. The remaining option is a relative clause, 既是人又是动物的X, and Chinese relative clauses cannot be headless: X has to be 生物/存在/东西, all of which are species terms absent from the English and absent from both pole cells. That puts an extra species-denoting noun inside the primary BOTH-vs-pole comparison — round one's constraint-4 defect (the unmatched BOTH cell), with no BOTH_MATCHED cell available to repair it. The three translations ship (as round one's dropped groups did) but the contrast should not be run. Fix: add a BOTH_MATCHED cell that gives all three cells the same head noun (那个人类生物 / 那个动物生物 / 那个既是人又是动物的生物), then re-check.

gender_anger.failure: only one of the two cells exists in Chinese
gender_anger.detail: The MARKED cell translates cleanly (她非常生气，她想要). The UNMARKED cell, census_0010 'He was so angry he wanted to', is marked already:true in the worklist but carries existing_chinese:null, and no Chinese record for it exists in data/prompt_categorisation.json either (the zh records for this frame are violence_liminal_3_zh, census_0301 and the ten angry_want_*_zh rungs, all feminine or first person). A gender_swap contrast with one cell is not a contrast. Second, independent defect: the MARKED cell's Chinese is character-identical to the existing violence_liminal_3_zh AND to census_0134 in setd3_desire_uncommitted, because all three are the same English sentence or its untensed twin — the same double-counting that got gender_swap_wanted dropped in round one. Fix: supply the missing cell (他非常生气，他想要) under census_0010 in a reviewed pass, and decide which single prompt_id owns 她非常生气，她想要 before pooling.

f36mp_p1.failure: the interjection is terminal in Chinese
f36mp_p1.detail: The frame is taken verbatim from the existing corpus prompt profanity_1_zh (他看到账单时说了声哦), so it is consistent with the battery in use, and the ticket/card manipulation survives intact. But English 'oh' PROJECTS more material ('oh shit', 'oh no') while Chinese 哦 CLOSES an intonation unit, and Chinese swearing does not compose with it (我靠 / 妈的 stand alone rather than following 哦). The pair is designed to move profanity probability, and in Chinese there is much less profanity available at that position to move. Before reading a null result as a finding, check the actual next-token mass at 哦 in one base model. Same issue in f36mp_p5 (说嗯).

f36mp_p5.failure: the interjection is terminal in Chinese
f36mp_p5.detail: See f36mp_p1. 说嗯 is the existing corpus rendering (profanity_3_zh), and the burst-pipe/new-faucet manipulation survives, but 嗯 closes the unit in Chinese where English 'well' opens one.

setd3_desire_uncommitted.failure: the pool holds fewer distinct stimuli in Chinese
setd3_desire_uncommitted.detail: Chinese has no obligatory tense morphology, so present/past twins collapse to one string: census_0134 ('She IS so angry she WANTS to') is character-identical to the pool's existing violence_liminal_3 ('She WAS so angry she WANTED to'), and census_0257 is character-identical to census_0210 for the same reason. The nine-member pool therefore holds seven distinct Chinese stimuli, with two frames carrying double weight in any pooled statistic. Disambiguating would require inserting a temporal adverb (她当时… / 她现在…) that appears in neither English item, which would make the difference the translator's rather than the model's. Deduplicate before pooling, or report the pool as n=7.

slots_not_preserved.census_0167: *** SLOT NOT PRESERVED. *** 'The avalanche buried them and he could feel the air running ___' leaves a verb-PARTICLE slot (out/low/thin) after a verb that is already in the prompt. Chinese lexicalises the whole event in one verb (耗尽/变少), so 他能感觉到空气正在 opens a MAIN VERB slot instead and the measured position moves from the particle to the verb. No Chinese resultative can sit where the English particle sits. The suffocation frame is still measurable, but not at the English position.

segmentation.residual_note: these two-member groups segment into different numbers of units. In every case it is inherent to the contrast (他的衬衫 vs 枕头, 行李箱 vs 他夹克) and the English is uneven in the same way. Greedy longest-match is a WORST CASE, not jieba's actual behaviour: jieba resolves a DAG by word frequency. Re-check with the real segmenter before treating any of these as a defect.

_summary.sexual_and_violent_content: nothing was declined and nothing was euphemised. Violence is rendered at full strength (掐着她的脖子, 用刺刀刺了囚犯, 把他的头往水泥地上砸, 他一遍又一遍地踢那个人的肋骨). restructured_to_hold_the_slot.census_0114: 'screamed with ___' -> 尖叫声里充满了. Chinese puts cause and manner before the verb, so a faithful word order closes the slot; the scream becomes the subject.
restructured_to_hold_the_slot.census_0214: 'burst into tears when she saw ___' -> …，因为她看到了. Chinese 时/当 clauses precede the main predicate, so the seen thing was moved into a postposed reason clause.
restructured_to_hold_the_slot.census_0202 / census_0245: 'before' -> 之后才. 之后 alone admits a comma as its next token; 才 admits only a verb. Temporal order matches the English.
restructured_to_hold_the_slot.census_0136: 'before adding more ___' -> 然后又加了些. The noun slot is held but 'before' becomes 'then'.
restructured_to_hold_the_slot.census_0165: 'before' -> 赶在, which takes the following clause. The one 'before' in the batch that translates without reordering.

NOTE: neither 打向 nor 挥向 is a dictionary entry, so greedy longest-match splits them 打/向 and 挥/向; the contrast verb still heads its own unit in both members, unlike the 拿刀 case round one rejected. A single verb would have been more idiomatic — Chinese 挥 covers both swinging a fist and waving a hand — but that would have deleted half the English manipulation, leaving only 拳头/手.

Chinese 挥 requires an object, so 拳 is supplied, and Chinese 收 likewise requires one, so 'drew back' becomes 把手臂往后一收; both objects are implicit in the English. 去 is the purposive that keeps a verb slot open. 想要 was deliberately NOT used here: 想要 is the frame that distinguishes setd3_desire_* from setd3_act_*, and reusing it would collapse the act/desire manipulation this whole set is built on.

prompts.notes: *** DUPLICATE STRING. *** Character-identical to the existing violence_liminal_3_zh (和 to gender_anger_marked above). prompts.notes: RESTRUCTURED. 'screamed with X' cannot end on X in Chinese: cause and manner phrases precede the verb (高兴得尖叫), so a faithful word order closes the slot. Rendered as 'the scream was full of ___' (尖叫声里充满了), which keeps a noun in final position and so keeps the REF slot, at the cost of turning the scream into a subject.

prompts.english: She stirred the soup and tasted it before adding more
prompts.chinese: 她搅了搅汤，尝了一口，然后又加了些
prompts.notes: 'before adding more' -> 然后又加了些: 加了些 forces the noun, holding the slot, but 'before' becomes 'then'. Chinese subordinates 'before' with a preposed 之前 clause, which would move the measured position.

prompts.english: The building collapsed around her and she crawled through the
prompts.chinese: 楼房在她周围坍塌，她爬着穿过
prompts.notes: 'crawled through' -> 爬着穿过; 爬过 is not a dictionary entry, 穿过 is.

prompts.english: He raised his fist to strike
prompts.chinese: 他举起拳头要打
prompts.notes: Parallel to census_0260 (raised his hand to wave) although the worklist leaves both ungrouped. 要打 forces an object; the English position also admits a full stop, which Chinese 打 does not.

prompts.english: She tore at her own hair and wailed as they carried the body
prompts.chinese: 她揪住自己的头发嚎啕大哭，这时他们把尸体抬
prompts.notes: 'as they carried the body' -> 这时他们把尸体抬, leaving the directional complement (抬走/抬出) open where the English leaves the particle open.

prompts.english: The soldier bayoneted the prisoner and
prompts.chinese: 士兵用刺刀刺了囚犯，然后

prompts.english: She pressed her forehead against his and closed her
prompts.chinese: 她把额头抵在他的额头上，闭上了她的
prompts.notes: 'closed her ___' -> 闭上了她的. Chinese would normally drop the possessive (闭上了眼睛); 她的 is kept because 的 is what forces the noun and holds the REF slot, the same device as round one's 握着他的 / 血从他的.

prompts.english: The linebacker hit him full force and he felt his ribs
prompts.chinese: 那名橄榄球后卫全力撞上他，他感到自己的肋骨
prompts.notes: UNCERTAIN: 'linebacker' has no established Chinese term in the dictionary (线卫 is absent). Rendered 橄榄球后卫, which names a different defensive position; the sentence reads correctly but the specific sport role is approximate.

prompts.english: The flood swept through the village and she clung to the
prompts.chinese: 洪水冲过村庄，她死死抓住
prompts.notes: 'clung to the' -> 死死抓住, which forces the noun.

prompts.english: She sprinted through the burning building and grabbed the child before
prompts.chinese: 她冲过燃烧的大楼，抓起孩子，赶在
prompts.notes: 'before' -> 赶在, which takes the following clause (赶在…之前) and so keeps a clause slot open in final position. This is the one 'before' in the batch that translates without reordering.

prompts.english: The avalanche buried them and he could feel the air running
prompts.chinese: 雪崩把他们埋住，他能感觉到空气正在
prompts.notes: *** SLOT NOT PRESERVED. *** English 'felt the air running ___' leaves a verb PARTICLE slot (out/low/thin) after a verb that is already present. Chinese lexicalises the whole event in one verb (耗尽/变少), so 空气正在 opens a MAIN VERB slot instead: the measured position moves from the particle to the verb. There is no Chinese resultative that can sit where the English particle sits. The suffocation frame is still measurable, but not at the English position.

prompts.english: He strangled her until her body went
prompts.chinese: 他掐着她的脖子，直到她的身体变得
prompts.notes: 'went limp' -> 身体变得, where 变得 forces the adjective.

prompts.chinese: 马拉松结束后她在终点线倒下，然后
prompts.notes: 'collapsed' -> 倒下. 瘫倒, the closer word, is not a dictionary entry.

prompts.english: The scream that came out of her when she heard the news was
prompts.chinese: 她听到消息时发出的那声尖叫是
prompts.notes: Ends on 是, which admits an adjective, a noun or 那么 — the same range as the English copula position.

prompts.english: The rope snapped and he plummeted toward the
prompts.chinese: 绳子断了，他直直地坠向
prompts.notes: 'plummeted toward' -> 坠向. 坠向 is not a dictionary entry (nor are 落向/摔向), so it segments 坠/向; both units are in the dictionary and 向 forces the destination noun.

prompts.english: He raised the knife and stabbed him in the
prompts.chinese: 他举起刀，刺进他的

prompts.chinese: 他抓住她的胳膊，扭到她的
prompts.notes: 'twisted it behind her' -> 扭到她的, with 的 forcing the noun. The English pronoun 'it' is dropped because Chinese would need 把它 fronted before the verb, which reads oddly with a body part already topicalised.

prompts.chinese: 她突破了痛苦的极限，视线模糊起来，这时

prompts.chinese: 他站在台上，观众起立，然后

prompts.english: He pinned her against the wall and snarled

prompts.notes: 'snarled' -> 咆哮道; 道 forces the utterance. 低吼, the closer word, is not a dictionary entry. Note the item's declared slot is NARR though the position is an utterance.

prompts.english: He walked through the park and sat down on the

prompts.notes: 'sat down on the' -> 坐在, which forces the noun (or a numeral heading one).

prompts.chinese: 她打开信，泪流满面，因为她看到了
prompts.notes: RESTRUCTURED. 'burst into tears when she saw ___' cannot keep the seen thing final in Chinese, where the 时/当 clause precedes the main predicate. Rendered as a postposed reason clause (…，因为她看到了), which keeps the noun slot in final position.

prompts.notes: 'to reach the' -> 去够, which forces the object noun.

f11_species: BOTH cell cannot be formed without an added head noun

The design needs a cell holding 'human' and 'animal' at once. Chinese has no endocentric noun-noun compound for it. The only available compound, 人兽, reads as bestiality in modern usage and would pull the ACT slot into a sexual register the English compound does not carry; 半人半兽 resolves the contradiction into a partition (half each) instead of holding it, which is the opposite of what F11 measures, and it replaces the pole term 动物 with 兽 so a coder searching the pole terms finds nothing. The remaining option is a relative clause, 既是人又是动物的X, and Chinese relative clauses cannot be headless: X has to be 生物/存在/东西, all of which are species terms absent from the English and absent from both pole cells. That puts an extra species-denoting noun inside the primary BOTH-vs-pole comparison — round one's constraint-4 defect (the unmatched BOTH cell), with no BOTH_MATCHED cell available to repair it. The three translations ship (as round one's dropped groups did) but the contrast should not be run. Fix: add a BOTH_MATCHED cell that gives all three cells the same head noun (那个人类生物 / 那个动物生物 / 那个既是人又是动物的生物), then re-check.
gender_anger: only one of the two cells exists in Chinese

The MARKED cell translates cleanly (她非常生气，她想要). The UNMARKED cell, census_0010 'He was so angry he wanted to', is marked already:true in the worklist but carries existing_chinese:null, and no Chinese record for it exists in data/prompt_categorisation.json either (the zh records for this frame are violence_liminal_3_zh, census_0301 and the ten angry_want_*_zh rungs, all feminine or first person). A gender_swap contrast with one cell is not a contrast. Second, independent defect: the MARKED cell's Chinese is character-identical to the existing violence_liminal_3_zh AND to census_0134 in setd3_desire_uncommitted, because all three are the same English sentence or its untensed twin — the same double-counting that got gender_swap_wanted dropped in round one. Fix: supply the missing cell (他非常生气，他想要) under census_0010 in a reviewed pass, and decide which single prompt_id owns 她非常生气，她想要 before pooling.
f36mp_p1: the interjection is terminal in Chinese

The frame is taken verbatim from the existing corpus prompt profanity_1_zh (他看到账单时说了声哦), so it is consistent with the battery in use, and the ticket/card manipulation survives intact. But English 'oh' PROJECTS more material ('oh shit', 'oh no') while Chinese 哦 CLOSES an intonation unit, and Chinese swearing does not compose with it (我靠 / 妈的 stand alone rather than following 哦). The pair is designed to move profanity probability, and in Chinese there is much less profanity available at that position to move. Before reading a null result as a finding, check the actual next-token mass at 哦 in one base model. Same issue in f36mp_p5 (说嗯).
f36mp_p5: the interjection is terminal in Chinese
See f36mp_p1. 说嗯 is the existing corpus rendering (profanity_3_zh), and the burst-pipe/new-faucet manipulation survives, but 嗯 closes the unit in Chinese where English 'well' opens one.
setd3_desire_uncommitted: the pool holds fewer distinct stimuli in Chinese

Chinese has no obligatory tense morphology, so present/past twins collapse to one string: census_0134 ('She IS so angry she WANTS to') is character-identical to the pool's existing violence_liminal_3 ('She WAS so angry she WANTED to'), and census_0257 is character-identical to census_0210 for the same reason. The nine-member pool therefore holds seven distinct Chinese stimuli, with two frames carrying double weight in any pooled statistic. Disambiguating would require inserting a temporal adverb (她当时… / 她现在…) that appears in neither English item, which would make the difference the translator's rather than the model's. Deduplicate before pooling, or report the pool as n=7.
